input.question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick
input.ground_truth: Because it can. Moving from extreme temperatures one to another can weaken your immune system and that makes it easier for you to get sick. So while it won't directly make you sick to be out in the cold, going between temps is what will do it. Unless it's something like hypothermia. That can make you sick just from being out in the cold.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you are a little teddy bear. When you get cold and wet, you start to shiver, right? Sometimes, when people get very cold (like being outside in freezing weather or swimming in icy water), their bodies have to work extra hard to stay warm.

When your body is cold, it can be easier for germs (tiny invisible bugs that can make you sick) to sneak in and make you feel yucky. Also, when you are cold, your nose might get stuffy and your throat might feel scratchy, and that can feel like you are getting sick.

But actually, just being cold by itself doesn’t make you sick. It’s usually germs that make you sick. However, being cold can make it easier for those germs to bother you. That’s why some people think being cold can make you sick!
